question: A physical instructor claims that the mean weight of students in school is greater than 82 kg with standard deviation 20. If a sample of size 81 students is selected with mean weight of 90. The test statistic equals to
solution:
The correct answer is** z = 3.6**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **test statistic** is a measure of the difference between the sample mean and the population mean in terms of standard deviations.
 
• In this case, the test statistic can be calculated as follows:
 
 
• z = (sample mean - population mean) / (standard deviation / sqrt(sample size))
 
• z = (90 - 82) / (20 / sqrt(81))
 
• z = 3.6
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **test statistic** is a measure of the difference between the sample mean and the population mean in terms of standard deviations.
 
• The test statistic is calculated by dividing the difference between the sample mean and the population mean by the standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size.
 
• The test statistic can be used to determine the significance of the difference between the sample mean and the population mean.
 
• If the test statistic is large enough, it can be concluded that the sample mean is significantly different from the population mean.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] ​ **Important Points__**

 
• The test statistic
 
 
• It is only meaningful if the sample is a random sample.
 
• It assumes that the population is normally distributed.
 
• It is only one piece of information used to make inferences about the population mean.
 
 
• Other factors, such as the sample size and the variability of the population, must also be taken into account.
